newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen weak at start.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen weak at start.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open lower Monday after a rise in the long bond yield and a selloff in the Dow industrials shook markets last week.
Analysts said some program selling was likely at the start but stocks could see a rebound during the day.
February personal income rose a higher than forecast 0.9 percent, while consumption rose a smaller than forecast 0.3 percent, according to government figures.
"People are on edge after Thursday's decline," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
"The data will keep the market on the defensive. If the numbers continue to strengthen, it will raise questions about when the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates again.

"There may be some program selling at the start, but bargain-hunting should come in later in the session. The fact that the market snapped back some after being down more than 200 points Thursday is positive. It shows there are buyers."
Shiva Corp shares are expected to take a beating after the company said its first quarter earnings and revenues would fall short of analysts' views.
